narrative.text:
“Fix round 4 for TASK-V1DZF.” I’ll read the full re-review and probes, add the strict diagnostic choke point and detached native-object projections, then rerun the required checks on both engines.The new regressions reproduce both findings. Native projection tests pass after the copy fix, and the final-message path covers the reproduced handshake, pagination, and reconnect failures. It also exposed a compatibility question: whole-message redaction masks parts of the fixed `metadata-credential` reason code for short credentials. I’ll ask the manager how to preserve that code while continuing the boundary audit.The manager approved preserving compile-time SDK reason codes, provided they are structurally separate from reflected text—not recognized by matching text in a message. I’ll use typed fields for those codes, keep the 94-character control passing, and add coverage for forged marker text containing the credential.The new regression tests pass, and the unchanged 94-character credential probe still passes. The choke point now receives fixed SDK reason codes separately from message text, so server-forged marker text gets no exemption. I’m finishing the diagnostic-site inventory before the clean-commit checks and legacy comparisons.All required checks pass at the clean final commit: 96 focused tests on each engine, all reviewer probe reruns, both legacy comparison variants on both engines, build, typecheck, and the full suite (7,955 tests; zero failures). I’m recording the inventory and evidence report before finalizing.The inventory found three secondary diagnostic paths still outside the choke point: trace-listener errors, webhook failures, and a reference-registration callback. I’ve routed them through it and added real-response-backed callback coverage. On the starting source, the final new tests produce eight expected failures and eight passing controls on each engine. All checks are rerunning at the latest commit.The manager requires a committed mechanical closure test that enumerates every relevant Error, throw, console, event/trace, ops-alert and failure-log site, failing unless it routes through the choke point or has a reasoned allowlist entry. I’ll add that now. The separate fixed-code instruction is already implemented and tested: only typed SDK constants are preserved; reflected marker text is redacted normally.The manager approved delivering the allowlist as explicitly unreviewed proposals. I must group it by reason, separately list every potentially server/peer/provider-derived site, and give each deferred-boundary entry a named downstream boundary and a test covering that site’s output. I’ll document those links and the scan’s limits, then finalize.The guard now enumerates 740 sites: 258 locally routed sites and 482 explicitly unreviewed proposals, including audit/log callbacks and process-event publications. A boundary-witness test covers all 355 deferred/root proposals with current and retained credentials; the report will list potentially peer-derived entries separately.

The first combined focused run exposed shared failures.log interference from the new tests. I isolated their log writes in temporary working directories; all 104 focused tests then passed on both engines. The final gates are rerunning at the new clean commit.Correction: the witness test covers **339** deferred/root proposals; **373** entries are conservatively marked potentially peer-derived.

The clean rerun found the same record-count race between two older TASK-V1DZF test files sharing failures.log. I’ll isolate those fixtures too, keeping their exact-count assertions intact, then rerun the gates.All final checks pass at `f2df7e41`: 104 focused tests on each engine, build, typecheck, all reviewer probes, both legacy byte-comparison variants, and the full suite (7,963 tests; zero failures). The mechanical guard has no unlisted sites in its stated scope. The 482 exception proposals remain explicitly unreviewed, with all 373 potentially peer-derived entries listed separately for the reviewer. I’m saving the final report and finalizing.The manager asks for the count and named entries of potentially received-data exceptions without redaction-boundary test coverage, grouped by reason, and for the scan limits inside the committed test file. I’ll report **34 operational-data proposals** in that category, separately from the **339 deferred/root proposals** with named boundary witnesses. The latter tests still do not prove each original site’s delegation. I’ll add the test-file limits comment and rerun the gates.
